title: Miami Spice Back with New Reserve Tier and 300 Restaurants

whatHappening: Miami Spice Restaurant Month is returning for its 25th edition, running from August 1 through September 30, 2026. The program now features a new reserve tier and will include more than 300 participating restaurants offering three-course prix-fixe menus with minimum savings of 30%.
whoInvolved: The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) is organizing the event, the official tourism and convention authority for the Miami area. The program involves over 300 restaurants across the Miami region participating in the promotional dining initiative.
whyMatters: Miami Spice drives significant restaurant traffic and consumer spending during the slower summer months, boosting the hospitality sector when tourism typically dips. The expansion to 300 restaurants and introduction of a premium reserve tier signals growing interest in fine dining deals and reflects the region's competitive restaurant landscape.
articleBody:
Miami's most anticipated dining event is making a comeback. The 25th edition of Miami Spice Restaurant Month will run from August 1 through September 30, 2026, offering diners across the region an opportunity to experience three-course prix-fixe menus at participating establishments with savings of at least 30%. According to Miami Curated, the Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) is expanding the program this year with the introduction of a new reserve tier, adding another dimension to the already popular promotion.

The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau has long used Miami Spice as a cornerstone event for stimulating dining activity during the summer months, traditionally a slower period for the hospitality industry. By negotiating set-price menus with restaurants across the city—from casual neighborhood spots to upscale fine dining establishments—the GMCVB creates an accessible entry point for both locals and visitors to explore new restaurants without breaking their budgets.

This year's expansion reflects the maturity and success of the program over its quarter-century run. With more than 300 restaurants participating, the 2026 edition represents substantial growth in both the number of establishments involved and the diversity of dining experiences available. The introduction of a reserve tier suggests the program is segmenting its offerings, likely to appeal to diners seeking premium experiences while maintaining the original mission of making fine dining more affordable.

The timing of Miami Spice remains strategically important for the region's restaurant community. August and September are months when Miami typically experiences reduced tourism due to summer heat and hurricane season considerations, making the promotional push valuable for maintaining revenue and customer engagement. For diners, the event provides a compelling reason to visit restaurants they might otherwise hesitate to try, potentially creating new regular customers for participating establishments.

As the 25th iteration takes shape, Miami Spice continues to evolve while maintaining its core appeal: exceptional dining value during a season that needs it most. The program's longevity and expansion suggest both strong participation from restaurants and consistent demand from the dining public.

whoInvolved: Miami Curated, a lifestyle publication focusing on the Miami area, has curated this list. articleBody:
Miami's bar scene is drawing inspiration from iconic establishments that have defined luxury hospitality for decades. According to Miami Curated, one standout reference point is the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis in New York City, a venue that evokes the elegance of a bygone era when refined living was the cultural standard. The writer notes that stepping into such spaces feels like an immersion into a time when sophisticated atmosphere was deeply valued, even as contemporary fashion and lifestyle trends have shifted decidedly toward the casual.

The St. Regis New York, located at 2 East 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, has been synonymous with luxury since its completion in 1904. Designed by Trowbridge & Livingston and later expanded with an annex by Sloan & Robertson in 1927, the hotel remains operated by Marriott International and maintains both Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings. The King Cole Bar within it has long served as a touchstone for what elevated hospitality looks like—a standard against which other luxury venues are measured.

Miami's featured establishments appear to draw from this same playbook of timeless elegance. Rather than chasing fleeting trends, these bars seem to prioritize atmospherics, service quality, and an intentional design language that harks back to an earlier era of hospitality. The piece suggests that even as modern culture has embraced casualness in dress and manners, there remains a distinct clientele seeking spaces where formality, refinement, and a sense of occasion still hold sway.

The tension between casual modernity and classical elegance forms the underlying theme of the curated list. The author acknowledges that fashion has moved away from the formal, yet establishments that maintain these old-world standards continue to thrive and attract patrons. This durability suggests that the desire for elegance and sophisticated environments has not disappeared—it has simply become more selective and intentional, appealing to those who value such experiences.

whatHappening: Paperfish Sushi Brickell has elevated its dining experience beyond its casual lunch and happy hour roots, stepping up its game to offer more serious dinner service. articleBody:
Paperfish Sushi Brickell has long held a place in the casual dining rotation for Miami professionals seeking a quick lunch or after-work happy hour. But according to Miami Curated, the restaurant has now made a deliberate move to establish itself as a serious dinner destination, expanding beyond its reputation as a convenient midday spot.

The transformation builds on what has always been the restaurant's strongest asset: its inviting décor that creates an immediate sense of warmth and brightness upon entering. That aesthetic foundation has made Paperfish a reliable choice for casual gatherings, but the restaurant is now leveraging that same appeal to draw a dinner crowd looking for more than just convenience.

Brickell's character as Miami's financial district has created a particular dynamic in its dining scene. Located directly east of Interstate 95 and south of the Central Business District, the neighborhood draws both weekday workers and weekend visitors, creating distinct dining cycles. Restaurants that can serve both the rapid-fire lunch market and the more leisurely dinner scene have a significant competitive advantage in this location.

In a sushi market crowded with options across Miami, Paperfish's decision to emphasize its dinner service represents a strategic move to differentiate itself. The restaurant recognizes that while many competitors vie for the lunch business, there is opportunity in serving customers who want a more complete evening experience, with the time and ambiance to enjoy their meal.

The restaurant's evolution also reflects changing expectations among Miami diners, particularly in Brickell where business professionals and residents increasingly seek quality venues for both work meals and personal celebrations. By stepping up its game for dinner service, Paperfish is positioning itself to capture that broader market while maintaining the loyalty of its existing casual crowd.
